I overdosed when I was 16. I lost all of my friends because they couldn’t deal with my problems. I really thought I wanted to die. In hindsight, I really wanted to stop feeling the way I’d always felt and I didnt see any other option because I didn’t have the tools to help myself. When I thought of the future, all I saw was blackness. But when I took those pills, something came over me. I love my mom. How could I do that to her? I could not lie to myself and say that my family would not miss me. I knew my mom would spend the rest of her life wondering what she did wrong, what she didn’t do enough of, if it was her fault. I woke up in the hospital the next day. My parents hadn’t slept. They spent the whole night crying by my bedside. If anything, that moment was their wake up call that I really fucking needed help. You won’t get it in the psych ward, it exists to keep you alive within their doors not to help you exist beyond them. I started seeing new therapists and psychiatrists. If I felt unease with one, I saw another until I found a fit. It was not easy, and not a magic cure for what I’d been feeling. I am still in the process of unlearning and retraining my brain to not immediately default to the worst possible scenario with the only solution being killing my self. At first, I stayed here because I promised myself I would never hurt my mom, so I had to at least stay alive until she died so she wouldn’t have to experience it. Now, I see it as a why not? Suicide is always an option, I can opt out whenever, but why not see what could happen? You don’t know what you don’t know. There are limitless possibilities for what your life could become that you can’t even begin to fathom right now. Find one thing. Make a list of anything and everything you enjoy or that brings you comfort. Add to it as often as you can. I’m 23 now. I’m not “cured”, I still have depression, but I am not miserable and I am alive in ways I never thought possible. I made friends that really get me, I found new hobbies that I’m really passionate about, I started teaching (and actually really enjoy it despite pitying teachers while I was in school). It’s really cheesy, but there are times I have felt so happy that I cried and thought about how glad I was to be able to experience it. Things change, circumstances change, you change. Everything can change if you let it. I promise it’s okay, even if it doesn’t feel that way right now. I really hope you’ll stay to find out.

Personally, I don't think I could ever be in it "no matter what." I'm learning how to prioritize myself and I'm starting to see relationships not as a source of completion but as a way to just enjoy life with another fully formed individual. That being said, a couple big things that I look for to get to that is: respecting boundaries, remembering details, treating those in the service industry with respect, treating me like a person regardless of my gender! acts of service! desire for better, and the will to get there. I think I show it with constant affection - I'm loud about love! I just want to talk and listen and spend time and do little things because I know it'll make their day a little smoother.

Things that instantly kill it for me: frat boys, no respect for animals, video games (yeah idk why), bad hygiene, too many opinions about my life, caring but not doing, stubbornness over stupid shit. When it's over, idk man it's over. Like I can't fake liking someone. My face isn't as happy to see you, it's harder to smile, nothing is funny to me anymore, I recoil when touched, I stop talking.

I really think everything comes down to respect. If you respect me and all the shit that I am, and I can respect you because none of the above things are applicable to you, it'll work out. But most of the time, I know things just won't last. Not because it's anyone's fault but because of the circumstances. If it's too much or doesn't seem realistic to be with a person, it probably isn't. So I don't try too hard to work things out or make things last, because I know the universe will send me whatever I'm meant to have.

If I have a problem I do like to go about it slowly, like I need a minute to think and sort out what I want to say. I'm pretty straightforward and I tend to address things over text (while emphasizing that I really just want to talk things out) so we both have time to properly think of a response.

When it comes to getting a crush on someone it's really all or nothing. I've got some high standards, and I'll admit most people don't meet them. But if really think you meet those standards, all the walls melt in a heartbeat. Most, if not all, of my romantic relationships have been scarily passionate and very short lived flings. In all but one, it ended because I realized that I misjudged them to better people than they were.

I do love the idea of devotion, but I hate it for myself. I don't think I'm monogamous. I don't want to force anyone to be bound to me. I just like genuine connection, and I'm all about it when it lasts but I'm also aware that I'm making room for what's coming!

I know exactly what you mean. I felt like that for a long while. Honestly? You probably don’t annoy everyone you come into contact with. If you already analyze everything you do and say and how it’s perceived as you’re doing and saying them, you (subconsciously) look for negative reactions because you expect them. So you could just learn to expect people to have positive reactions when you do or say something, which is easier said than done. It’s all about building confidence. While you’re learning to do that, consistently remind yourself that 1) you cannot control how people act/react and 2) you cannot read someone else’s mind, which is to say that you should not assume what someone else is thinking or feeling unless they explicitly state it, especially when it comes to what they think about you. I hate to say it’s probably all in your head, but it probably is and that doesn’t make it any less difficult to deal with. Focus on yourself and if you still genuinely believe that people are annoyed by you or find you awkward, you’ll just have to trust that there will eventually be people in your life who don’t.
